description: Validates the Memory Optimizer (REM dreaming) prompt — Stage A.1 hub decomposition with RED ZONE rule, Stage A.2 island bridging. Sandbox mode: agent describes commands it would run on mock graph output; judge checks behavior.

evals.name: red-zone-hub-not-skipped
evals.expected_output: Tackles person_anya FIRST (degree 71 = RED ZONE), decomposes via introduce-topic into themed sub-clusters, never marks it SKIP
expectations: Tackles person_anya FIRST, before topic_misc, because it has the larger active_degree (71 vs 22)
Recognizes person_anya as RED ZONE territory because active_degree >= 50
Calls codeterm mem graph introduce-topic with multiple sources to break person_anya into themed sub-clusters
Does NOT mark person_anya as SKIP citing reasons like 'too big to handle now', 'this is a person of course they have many facts', or 'will get to it next run'
Considers re-calling mem graph hubs with --sample 100 (or higher) to see all 71 neighbor titles before declaring there's no structure

evals.name: biggest-hub-first
evals.expected_output: Picks machine_blackstar first because it has the larger active_degree
expectations: Picks machine_blackstar (degree 60) first, before project_codeterm (degree 25)
Reason given is explicitly about hub size / active_degree / search-noise concentration, not arbitrary order
Does NOT pick project_codeterm first

evals.name: partial-decomposition-allowed
evals.prompt:
You're partway through Stage A.1 of REM. You've decomposed 4 hubs already and your token budget is tight — maybe enough for one more substantial action. The next hub is:

{
  "id": "project_codeterm",
  "active_degree": 70,
  "sample_neighbors": [
    {"title":"v1.1.20 release notes"}, {"title":"v1.1.21 release notes"}, {"title":"v1.1.22 release notes"},
    {"title":"build.sh dev script"}, {"title":"build.sh kill script"}, {"title":"./build.sh test workflow"},
    {"title":"mesh handshake protocol"}, {"title":"mesh peer pairing"}, {"title":"mesh discovery"},
    {"title":"telegram bridge config"}, {"title":"telegram allowed_users gotcha"},
    {"title":"mem graph hubs CLI"}, {"title":"mem graph islands CLI"}, {"title":"mem search FTS+vector"},
    {"title": "... 56 more neighbors"}
  ]
}

You're not sure you have time to decompose this fully. What do you do?
evals.expected_output: Pulls 3-5 themed sub-clusters via introduce-topic (release-history, dev-workflow, mesh, telegram, mem-graph) and logs as 'partially decomposed', does NOT skip entirely
expectations: Pulls at least 3 themed sub-clusters out of project_codeterm via codeterm mem graph introduce-topic (e.g. topic_release_history, topic_dev_workflow, topic_mesh, topic_telegram, topic_mem_graph)
Logs the action as 'partially decomposed' with residue count for the next REM run to pick up
Does NOT skip the hub entirely citing token budget, time pressure, or 'will continue next run' as a full skip
Does NOT mark this RED-ZONE hub (active_degree=70) as SKIPped — partial work still counts as progress

evals.name: homogeneous-low-degree-skip-ok
evals.prompt:
Stage A.1 of REM. mem graph hubs returned:

{
  "id": "learning_jwt_kid_header_required",
  "kind": "Learning",
  "active_degree": 22,
  "relation_types": {"extracted_from": 22},
  "sample_neighbors": [
    {"id": "conv_2026_03_15_a", "title": "Conversation 2026-03-15 (Auth0 debug session)"},
    {"id": "conv_2026_04_02_b", "title": "Conversation 2026-04-02 (JWT validation issue)"},
    {"id": "conv_2026_04_18_c", "title": "Conversation 2026-04-18 (production token rejection)"},
    {"title": "... 19 more conv_* snapshots, all extracted FROM this learning"}
  ]
}

Decompose this hub or skip it?
evals.expected_output: Skips it correctly with reason 'popular source, not a structural hub' — extracted_from edges are provenance pointers, not structure
expectations: Skips this hub with the reason 'popular source, not a structural hub' (or equivalent — provenance pointers via extracted_from, not structural decomposable themes)
Does NOT call introduce-topic on this hub
Does NOT try to invent themed sub-clusters for the conversation snapshots (they're provenance, not content)

evals.name: island-existing-anchor-relate-not-introduce
evals.expected_output: Uses codeterm mem graph relate (single edge) bridging one member into existing topic_auth — does NOT introduce-topic since the anchor already exists
expectations: Uses codeterm mem graph relate (single edge) to bridge a member of the island into the existing topic_auth anchor
Picks one most-central / first member as --from and topic_auth as --to
Does NOT call codeterm mem graph introduce-topic — that command is for inventing NEW topic anchors, not reusing existing ones
Does NOT try to invent a new topic_<theme> when topic_auth already covers the island

evals.name: hub-clusters-drive-introduce-topic-no-scripts
evals.expected_output: Decomposes person_mira first, one introduce-topic per cluster using suggested_topic, entity_type and members verbatim with --anchor person_mira, then tech_redis; never touches project_dreams and never writes a script or temp file.
expectations: Handles person_mira (degree 41) before tech_redis (degree 22)
Calls codeterm mem graph introduce-topic with --topic-id topic_mira_infra and --sources listing the four infra member ids from the cluster, with --anchor person_mira
Reuses topic_cooking (the existing suggested_topic) rather than inventing a new slug for the cooking cluster
Does NOT decompose or route anything into project_dreams (it is listed under excluded as the dreams anchor)
Does NOT use python, jq, a heredoc, a pipe, a shell variable, or a /tmp file to process the hubs JSON — every command is a plain codeterm invocation

evals.name: content-duplicate-merges-reversibly-never-deletes
evals.expected_output: One `codeterm mem merge --keeper fact_deploy_pipeline --lesser fact_deploy_pipeline_2 --body '<merged body>'` call carrying both facts; never `mem delete`; the diary log names the merged pair with a reason
expectations: Uses a single codeterm mem merge call with --keeper and --lesser naming the two items
Passes a merged keeper body that keeps both the notarization and the Windows signing facts
Does NOT call codeterm mem delete on either item
Logs the merged lesser and keeper ids with a short reason in the diary log (a MERGED line or equivalent)
